deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page continues a series of numerical solutions of the trinomial x^7 - 3x^2 + c = 0 for complex c. It is the 'fifth equation' and a 'Zugabe' (supplementary) equation; the previous page has the fourth equation. My observation, not stated on the page: the constants are c = (2-sqrt2) - sqrt2 i, (2+sqrt2) - sqrt2 i and (2-sqrt3) - i. All lie on the circle |c-2| = 2. The next page uses c = 2.0147191 = (15/7)(6/7)^(2/5), which is the real critical value of x^7 - 3x^2 (double root), and 4 - 2.0147191. So Gauss appears to be tracing how the roots move as c runs over curves he calls 'Parallelen', probably to draw a figure.

METHOD (Gauss's logarithmic-trigonometric solution of trinomials). Write c = |c| e^{iC}, put gamma = -C, and x = r e^{i phi}. Dividing by x^2 gives x^5 + c x^{-2} = 3. The three vectors x^5, c x^{-2} and -3 close a triangle. The law of sines gives:
- r^5 = 3 sin(2phi+gamma)/sin(7phi+gamma),
- |c| r^{-2} = 3 sin(5phi)/sin(7phi+gamma),
- hence r^7 = |c| sin(2phi+gamma)/sin(5phi).
Eliminating r gives the angle equation
 F(phi) = 7 log sin(7phi+gamma) - 2 log sin(2phi+gamma) - 5 log sin(5phi) = log(1/lambda), with 1/lambda = b^7/|c|^5 and b = 3.
This matches the next page's -lambda = sin^2(2R) sin^5(5R)/sin^7(7R). The beside-figures (+20.2, -5.8, ...) are tabular differences of log sin per 1'' in units of 1e-7. They are multiplied by 2*2, 5*5 and 7*7 to give dF/dphi. Each root is found by trial phi plus one linear interpolation (regula falsi / Newton step).

FIFTH EQUATION, c = 3.4142136 - 1.4142135 i.
- log sqrt2 = 0.1505150; log(2+sqrt2) = 0.5332907; log cos 22.5 deg = 9.9656153.
- tan(arg) = sqrt2/(2+sqrt2) = tan 22.5 deg, so C = 337 deg 30', gamma = 22.5 deg.
- log|c| = 0.5332907 - 9.9656153 = 0.5676753; log|c|^5 = 2.8383767; log 3^7 = 3.3398488.
- Target: log(1/lambda) = 3.3398488 - 2.8383767 = 0.5014721.

Root A. Trial phi = 11 deg 50'43'', so 2phi+gamma = 46 deg 11'26'', 5phi = 59 deg 13'35'', 7phi+gamma = 105 deg 25'1''.
- log sines: 9.8583243 (+20.2), 9.9340921 (+12.5), 9.9840846 (-5.8).
- 2x: 9.7166486 (+80.8); 5x: 9.6704605 (+312.5); sum 9.3871091 (+393.3).
- 7x: 9.8885922 (-284.2); F = 0.5014831 (-677.5).
- Required change -110, so dphi = +0.1624''; phi = 11 deg 50'43.162''.
- log r^7 = 9.8583243 - 9.9340921 = 9.9242322 (-22.1); corrected 9.9242318; plus log|c| gives 0.4919071.
- log r = 0.0702724; log cos phi = 9.9906519; log sin phi = 9.3123261.
- x = 1.1505997 + 0.2413229 i. An earlier value 1.1099621 + 0.2327997 i is struck out.

Root B. Trial phi = 172 deg 52'11'', angles 8 deg 14'22'', 144 deg 20'55'', 152 deg 35'17''.
- log sines: 9.1562774 (+145.4), 9.7655583 (-29.4), 9.6631210 (-40.6).
- Multiples: 8.3125548 (+581.6), 8.8277915 (-735.0); sum 7.1403463 (-153.4).
- 7x: 7.6418470 (-1989.4); F = 0.5015007 (-1836.0).
- Correction +286/1836 = 0.156''; phi = 172 deg 52'11.156''.
- log r^7 = 9.3907191 (+438), +68 gives 9.3907259; plus log|c| gives 9.9584012.
- log r = 9.9940573; log|cos| = 9.9966284 n; log sin = 9.0938597.
- x = -0.9787814 + 0.1224382 i.

Root C. Trial phi = 159 deg 12'50'', angles 340 deg 55'40'', 76 deg 4'10'', 56 deg 59'50''.
- log|sin|: 9.5142164 (-60.9), 9.9870376 (+5.2), 9.9235873 (+13.6).
- Multiples: 9.0284328 (-243.6), 9.9351880 (+130.0); sum 8.9636208 (-113.6).
- 7x: 9.4651111 (+666.4); F = 0.5014903 (+780.0).
- Correction -182/780 = -0.233''; phi = 159 deg 12'49.767''.
- log r^7 = 9.5271788 (-147.8), +34 gives 9.5271822. This ratio is negative because sin(2phi+gamma) < 0 and sin 5phi > 0.
- Therefore the true root is at phi+180 deg. That shift leaves F unchanged and makes r^7 positive. This is the role of the 'n' marks.
- log r^7 = 0.0948575, log r = 0.0135511, giving x = +0.9645447 - 0.3661245 i. I checked: x^5 + c x^{-2} = 3.

ZUGABE EQUATION, c = (2-sqrt3) - i = 0.2679... - i.
- log 1 = 0; log(2-sqrt3) = 9.4280525; log cos 15 deg = 9.9849438.
- log|c| = 0.0150562; C = 285 deg, so gamma = 75 deg.
- log|c|^5 = 0.0752810; log(1/lambda) = 3.2645678.

Root D. phi = 142 deg 23'54.5'', angles 359 deg 47'49'', 351 deg 59'32.5'', 351 deg 47'21.5''.
- log|sin|: 7.5494913 (-5941), 9.1439671 (-149.6), 9.1547698 (-146.0).
- 2x: 5.0989826 (-23764); 5x: 5.7198355 (-3740); sum 0.8188181 (-27504).
- 7x: 4.0833886 (-7154); F = 3.2645705 (+20350).
- Correction -27, so phi = 142 deg 23'54.499''.
- log r^7 = 8.4055242 (-11134), +15 gives 8.4055257; plus log|c| gives 8.4205819.
- log r = 9.7743688, giving x = -0.4712418 + 0.3629251 i.

Root E. phi = 142 deg 34'36'', angles 0 deg 9'12'', 352 deg 53'0'', 353 deg 2'12''.
- log|sin|: 7.4275134 (+7868), 9.0930367 (-168.6), 9.0836249 (-172.4).
- 2x: 4.8550268 (written +30672); 5x: 5.4651835 (-4215); sum 0.3202103 (+26457).
- 7x: 3.5853743 (-8447.6); F = 3.2651640 (-34904.6).
- Correction +5962/34904.6 = 0.171''.
- log r^7 = 8.3344767 (+16579), +2832 gives 8.3347599; plus log|c| gives 8.3498161.
- log r = 9.7642594. The ratio is negative (n), so the root is at phi+180 deg: x = +0.4614999 - 0.3531407 i.

NOTE AT BOTTOM. The 'Zugabe' points of the second parallel were:
- phi = 125 deg 25'13'', log r 9.70429, x = -0.29336 + 0.41249 i;
- phi = 306 deg 3'17'', log r 9.70440, x = +0.29798 - 0.40931 i.
They belong to '18 deg or 0.2', where log(1/lambda) = 3.91000, log|c| = 9.88597 and C = 251 deg 28'27''. This is consistent: 3.3398488 - 5(9.88597 - 10) = 3.91000. The Zugabe roots D and E are likewise a nearly antipodal pair, which suggests Gauss is locating where two roots come close together on the curves.
errors: Zugabe root E: the derivative of the 2 log sin(2phi+gamma) term should be 4*7868.0 = 31472, not 30672 (if the reading is right). The total derivative then becomes 27257 instead of 26457, and dF/dphi = -35704.6 instead of -34904.6. The correction would be 0.167'' rather than 0.171''. The effect on log r^7 is about 6e-6, i.e. about 1e-6 in the root: negligible.

Root B: the line written 9.3125548 for 2 log sin 8 deg 14'22'' should carry characteristic 8 (8.3125548), as the sum 7.1403463 shows. This is a characteristic slip or a misreading only; the subsequent work is correct.

Root C: the corrected angle should be 159 deg 12'49.767'' (trial 50'' minus 0.233''). The transcribed '159.12.50,1767' cannot be literally right; the sign used afterwards (+34 to log r^7) confirms the -0.233'' correction.
Struck-out first value of root A (1.1099621 + 0.2327997 i) has the right argument but wrong modulus. Gauss rejected it himself.

Otherwise all checked logarithms, tabular differences, interpolations and final roots agree to about 1e-7 in the logs. Substituting roots A and B back gives residuals at the 1e-4 level, which is the limit of my hand check, not an error in Gauss's values. Root C was verified via x^5 + c x^{-2} = 3.

results.what: Numerical solution of complex roots of the trinomial x^7 - 3x^2 + c = 0 (c complex) by the angle equation 7 log sin(7phi+gamma) - 2 log sin(2phi+gamma) - 5 log sin 5phi = log(3^7/|c|^5) and r^7 = |c| sin(2phi+gamma)/sin 5phi. Spurious solutions are rejected via sign ('n') and shifted by 180 deg.
results.modern_name: Gauss's logarithmic-trigonometric method for trinomial equations (law of sines on the root triangle)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Beitraege zur Theorie der algebraischen Gleichungen (1849/50), part on trinomial equations

results.what: Tracking the 7 roots as c moves along curves ('Parallelen') through the circle |c-2|=2 and near the critical value 2.0147191 = (15/7)(6/7)^(2/5), including pairs of nearby 'Zugabepunkte'.
results.modern_name: Numerical root-locus / monodromy-type study of a polynomial family near a branch point
results.usually_credited_to: Root-locus ideas: Puiseux/Riemann (1850s) conceptually; Evans (1948) for root locus in engineering

results.what: Linear interpolation using tabular log-sine differences per second to solve the transcendental angle equation
results.modern_name: Regula falsi / one Newton step with tabulated derivatives

deep.surprise_reason: The trigonometric method for trinomial roots is Gauss's own published method, and the page is routine (very accurate) table computation. The only mildly notable aspect is the systematic tracking of roots of x^7-3x^2+c along curves in the c-plane near a critical value. This is an unpublished computational exploration, but the purpose is not explicit on this page.
